newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY -- Many political and business figures who used to attend the celebration of Taiwan's Double Tenth national holiday did not show up at Thursday night's celebration.
-- Governor Chris Patten said he believed an agreement on the definition of Hong Kong permanent residents would be reached soon by China and Britain.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Activists campaigning for Chinese sovereignty over the Diaoyu (Senkaku) islands apologised for forcing their way into the Japanese consulate during a protest.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- A new hallucinatory drug called "White Angel" is poisoning teenagers in the Tuen Mun area.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The mother of Chinese dissident Wang Dan said she would defend her son in court if they failed to secure a lawyer within a day as the court had requested.

-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- A Communist Party plenum agreed that special organisations under the Central Committee and in the provinces and cities would be set up to strengthen efforts to build a "socialist spiritual civilisation".
-- Bejing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- China took economic measures to strengthen control over environmental protection.
-- Beijing's Number Two Chemical Factory is seeking a listing on the Hong Kong bourse.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The government said it might have to rely on the territory's chief executive-designate to force through the Mandatory Provident Fund if the scheme is delayed in the Legislative Council.
-- Pacific Concord has scaled down the issue size of its proposed property spin-off to US$120-150 million, against an initial expectation of $150-200 million.

-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- The People's Bank of China has issued an urgent circular ordering banks and other financial institutions to suspend new loans to car and home buyers to avoid chaos.
